name: Project Honey Pot http:BL (dnsbl.httpbl.org)
tier_rationale: Long-running community honeypot network with public API documentation and terms (A8 community).

reliability.justification: Visitor types and a log-scaled threat score from a distributed web honeypot network; scores age out with the last activity.

httpbl.description: Project Honey Pot http:BL access key (12 lower-case letters): embedded in the DNS query name, so it is only ever sent through the system resolver (never public DoH)
httpbl.plan_hint: record 'business' for the company account's key (key_plans.httpbl)

httpbl.title: Project Honey Pot http:BL (<key>.<reversed ip>.dnsbl.httpbl.org, DNS A 127.<days>.<score>.<type>)

terms.quote: P045 cond 1 (binding council text): Project Honey Pot http:BL is key-terms (company account).

httpbl.notes: Quote: binding council text (P045 cond 1); research C0378 (zone alive, NS ns1-3.httpbl.org). The access key sits in the query name: system resolver through dnspython only, never public DoH, query name redacted (P045 cond 3). NXDOMAIN = not listed; scores are log-scaled (P045 cond 9). Business use decided by key_plans.httpbl (company account). Used by dnsbl.

notes: Owned by batch p2-G02-2 (P045). DNS only: the list is queried through DNS A lookups (core DoH layer or the system resolver), never over HTTP, so the provider has no HTTP host. Every DNSBL counts as ONE 'spam' family vote in P171 consensus (upstream_family 'dnsbl', P045 cond 8).
